summary: Several added comments omit or contradict observable edge-case behavior, chiefly null handling and `Numeric.abs` overflow.

items.issue: The comment promises an absolute value, but the inherited implementation returns a negative value for the minimum signed primitive values: for example, `Numeric.IntIsIntegral.abs(Int.MinValue)` evaluates `negate(Int.MinValue)` and returns `Int.MinValue`. The same issue applies to `Long`, `Short`, and `Byte`.
items.suggestion: Document the fixed-width overflow case, or qualify the claim to the implementation's ordering-and-negation behavior.

items.issue: The base contract says invalid input produces `None`, but several documented built-in implementations (`IntIsIntegral`, `ShortIsIntegral`, `ByteIsIntegral`, `LongIsIntegral`, `FloatIsFractional`, and `DoubleIsFractional`) delegate to `StringParsers`, which dereferences a null `str` and throws `NullPointerException`. Their added comments repeat the same unconditional `None otherwise` claim.
items.suggestion: State that null input throws `NullPointerException` and add a corresponding `@throws` tag to the affected concrete methods; do not make the base contract promise `None` for every non-valid input unless all implementations satisfy it.

items.issue: The added exception documentation names division by zero but omits the material null case: evaluating `x / y` dereferences either `BigInt` operand and throws `NullPointerException` when it is null. `rem` has the same omission.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws NullPointerException` for null operands to both `quot` and `rem`, alongside the division-by-zero tag.

items.issue: The added docs for reference-valued operations such as `plus`, `minus`, `times`, `negate`, and the `toX` conversions omit their null failure behavior. Their bodies dereference the supplied `BigDecimal` values; the delegated `BigDecimal` operations also document `NullPointerException` for null operands.
items.suggestion: Document null handling with `@throws NullPointerException` on the affected methods, or explicitly make the methods null-safe if that is the intended contract.

items.issue: The `@throws` tag omits `NullPointerException` for a null divisor, although `x / y` immediately delegates to `BigDecimal./`, which dereferences `y.bigDecimal`. The tag similarly does not cover arithmetic failures caused by the receiver's `MathContext` (for example inexact division with `UNNECESSARY` rounding).
items.suggestion: Add the null exception and describe all documented `ArithmeticException` conditions of the delegated division rather than only zero divisors.

items.issue: Both `quot` and `rem` omit `NullPointerException` for a null divisor even though their `BigDecimal` delegates dereference it. Their arithmetic-exception tags also reduce the possible failure condition to zero divisors despite the `MathContext`-dependent delegated operations.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws NullPointerException` and state the additional `ArithmeticException` conditions supplied by the delegated `BigDecimal` operations.

items.issue: The inline code literals contain two backslashes (`'\\u0001'` and `'\\u0000'`), which do not denote the stated single `Char` values as Scala character literals.
items.suggestion: Render the values unambiguously, for example as `U+0001` and `U+0000`, or use single-backslash Scala escapes if safe for the Scaladoc source.

items.issue: This and many of the added comments use an `@return` tag that merely repeats a summary already beginning with “Returns”, contrary to the project convention.
items.suggestion: Remove redundant `@return` tags where the summary already completely describes the return value; retain tags that add edge-case information.

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing “without throwing” documentation is false for a null input: `parseByte` immediately calls `from.length()`. The same issue occurs in the other `StringParsers` numeric parsers.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Document `NullPointerException` for null input or make the parsers null-safe.
